title: English Usage · การเขียนข้อความทางการ

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Choose the clearest diplomatic request for a second review.
questions.answer: We would appreciate a further review of the proposal.
options: We would appreciate a further review of the proposal.
You are expected to stop and review it again immediately.
A further review may perhaps conceivably be considered by somebody.
questions.explanation: The first version identifies the requested action in courteous, direct language.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which sentence communicates a firm deadline politely?
questions.answer: Please send the signed copy by 4 p.m. on Tuesday.
options: Please send the signed copy by 4 p.m. on Tuesday.
You can send the signed copy whenever you get around to it.
By some point about Tuesday, the copy needs to exist.
questions.explanation: It states a specific deadline and a polite request.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which revision identifies who will verify the figures?
questions.answer: The audit team will verify the figures before publication.
options: The audit team will verify the figures before publication.
The figures will be verified before publication.
Before publication, verification will take place.
questions.explanation: Naming the audit team makes responsibility explicit.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which opening suits a short acknowledgement of an inquiry?
questions.answer: Thank you for your inquiry about the application deadline.
options: Thank you for your inquiry about the application deadline.
We read all kinds of emails every week.
Your timing is just about what we thought it would be.
questions.explanation: It acknowledges the inquiry and specifies its topic.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Choose the concise equivalent of “At this point in time, the decision has not yet been made.”
options: A decision is still pending.
The decision has already been announced.
It was decided long ago.
questions.explanation: “Pending” communicates that the decision is still outstanding.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Choose the sentence that attaches “only” to the named group.
questions.answer: Only registered participants may enter the room.
options: Only registered participants may enter the room.
Registered participants may only enter the room.
Registered participants may enter only after the session starts.
questions.explanation: Putting “only” before the group limits who may enter.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which revision avoids an unclear pronoun reference if the deputy sent the document?
questions.answer: After the meeting, the deputy sent the document to the chair.
options: After the meeting, the deputy sent the document to the chair.
The deputy met the chair, and she then sent the document.
After meeting the chair, it was sent by her.
questions.explanation: Naming the sender and recipient removes ambiguity.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Choose the neutral alternative to “The agency failed completely.”
questions.answer: The agency did not meet the stated targets.
options: The agency did not meet the stated targets.
The agency obviously ignored its duties.
The agency has always been unable to achieve anything.
questions.explanation: This version ties the statement to measurable targets.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which wording makes a requested attachment clear?
questions.answer: Please attach a copy of the signed agreement.
options: Please attach a copy of the signed agreement.
Please send the signed thing along with this if you have it.
Several documents may possibly be needed somewhere.
questions.explanation: It names the exact document to attach.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which language fits a short follow-up on an unanswered request?
questions.answer: I am following up on our request of 4 November.
options: I am following up on our request of 4 November.
You have had ages to respond.
A reply should already be here, obviously.
questions.explanation: It identifies the prior request without assuming a reason for the delay.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which version accurately conveys that one office remains open?
questions.answer: The central office will remain open during the regional closures.
options: The central office will remain open during the regional closures.
The central office will close during the regional closures.
All offices will remain open throughout the period.
questions.explanation: The exception is attached to the central office.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which sentence uses consistent list structure?
questions.answer: Check the form, sign the declaration, and submit both by Friday.
options: Check the form, sign the declaration, and submit both by Friday.
Check the form, signing the declaration, and submission by Friday.
The form is checked, sign the declaration, and submitted by Friday.
questions.explanation: All three instructions use the same base-verb form.
